title: Global peacefulness is deteriorating as conflicts diffuse across borders, militarization rises, and a fragmented power system weakens the conditions for peace
source_unit: Institute for Economics & Peace, Global Peace Index 2026: Measuring Peace in a Complex World
geography: 163 independent states and territories covering 99.7 percent of the world population, with comparisons across regions and three peace domains

denominator.unit: countries and territories ranked in the Global Peace Index 2026

peacefulness_change.unit: percent change in average global peacefulness over the past year

long_run_pattern.value: 2026 marks the 12th consecutive year of global peacefulness deterioration and the 15th deterioration in the last 18 years

observations.method: IEP Global Peace Index using 23 qualitative and quantitative indicators across societal safety and security, ongoing domestic and international conflict, and militarisation.
observations.uncertainty: The index is a composite ranking rather than a direct measure of lived safety, justice, or peace within every community; indicator selection and weighting shape the result.
observations.subgroup: Countries, regions, populations exposed to conflict or insecurity, governments, civil society, and institutions managing peace and security.
observations.counterinterpretation: Sixty-two countries improved and peacefulness can rise in particular regions or countries even during a global deterioration.

denominator.unit: global state-based conflict and conflict-death comparison frame

active_state_conflicts.unit: active state-based conflicts in the 2026 index assessment

external_conflict_countries_2008.unit: countries involved in at least one external conflict in the previous five years in 2008

external_conflict_countries_2026.unit: countries involved in at least one external conflict in the previous five years in the 2026 index

conflict_deaths_2024.unit: more than conflict deaths in 2024, the highest annual total in a generation according to the index summary

internal_conflict_change.value: global deaths from internal conflict rose more than sixfold from around 29,000 in 2008 to over 181,000 in the latest year reported

observations.method: IEP comparison of conflict, deaths, external involvement, and the ongoing-conflict domain within the Global Peace Index.
observations.uncertainty: Conflict counts and deaths depend on source coverage, definitions, attribution, and reporting; index figures should not be treated as complete event-level mortality records.
observations.subgroup: Civilians, combatants, countries involved in external conflicts, displaced populations, humanitarian actors, and communities exposed to internal violence.
observations.counterinterpretation: Conflict intensity and deaths can fall in individual theaters even while the number of conflicts or countries involved rises globally.

observations.period: 1991-2026; redistribution of power and geopolitical fragmentation

denominator.unit: IEP geopolitical-order and peace-system synthesis frame

structural_period.value: IEP identifies a Great Fragmentation beginning in the late 2000s after the Cold War and post-1990 globalisation periods

middle_powers_2026.unit: middle-power countries identified in the 2026 analysis

emerging_power_change.value: the number of emerging powers has tripled since 1991

capacity_shift.value: the combined material capacity of middle powers now exceeds that of the great powers in the report's framing

observations.method: IEP analysis connecting GPI trends with global power redistribution, middle powers, external conflict, militarisation, and international order.
observations.uncertainty: Terms such as great power, middle power, and material capacity depend on the report's analytical definitions and do not constitute a universal geopolitical taxonomy.
observations.subgroup: States, regional organizations, middle powers, great powers, smaller states, populations affected by external intervention, and diplomatic institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: A more plural distribution of power can create bargaining space and regional agency as well as fragmentation and escalation risk.

observations.period: 2026; measurement domains, economic cost, and positive peace

domains.value: societal safety and security, ongoing domestic and international conflict, and militarisation

indicator_count.unit: qualitative and quantitative indicators used by the index

economic_route.value: the report analyses the economic impact and value of peace alongside conflict and militarisation

positive_peace.value: attitudes, institutions, and structures that create and sustain peaceful societies are treated as a resilience pathway

observations.method: Composite index methodology and IEP analysis of peace, economic value, conflict spread, escalation hotspots, risk, and Positive Peace.
observations.uncertainty: Composite indicators identify patterns and associations; they do not establish that a single institution or attitude causes peace or that economic costs are identical across settings.
observations.subgroup: Public institutions, firms, households, communities, peacebuilders, security actors, and populations living with insecurity or militarisation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Index-based measurement can make peace capacity visible and support comparison, but local qualitative knowledge and community-level institutions may not be captured fully.

related_sources.claim: IEP interactive Global Peace Index 2026 site provides rankings, indicators, trends, and open-data context.
Official IEP Global Peace Index 2026 report PDF provides the detailed conflict, fragmentation, economic-impact, and methodology analysis.

boundary: This record adds a geopolitical peace route across peacefulness, conflict diffusion, conflict deaths, militarisation, power fragmentation, economic costs, and Positive Peace. It uses an aggregate IEP composite index and report synthesis, not respondent-level safety histories, event-level conflict microdata, individual victim records, causal geopolitical forecasts, or proof that index movement directly describes every community.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official IEP Global Peace Index 2026 landing page, interactive index page, report PDF, and methodology framing reviewed for rankings, 163-country scope, 23 indicators, three domains, peacefulness movement, conflict counts and deaths, power fragmentation, economic impact, and Positive Peace.
